days.name: Monday
days.curriculum: A Rose for Emily (Faulkner) — close reread of the opening; SPACE CAT graphic organizer.
days.learning_targets: I can describe the rhetorical situation of a text using SPACE CAT.
days.do_now: Cold-read the first paragraph of A Rose for Emily and write one sentence on the narrator's attitude toward Emily.
days.learning_looks_like:
Explicit: Model SPACE CAT on paragraph 1.
Student: Groups complete SPACE CAT for an assigned section.
Independent: Write a 4-sentence rhetorical-situation summary.
days.assessment: Formative — SPACE CAT organizer + summary paragraph.

days.name: Tuesday
days.curriculum: A Rose for Emily — diction & tone; DIDLS framework.
days.learning_targets: I can analyze how diction and detail create tone.
days.do_now: List three words from yesterday's reading that carry a strong connotation.
days.learning_looks_like:
Explicit: Model DIDLS on a key passage.
Student: Collaborative DIDLS annotation.
Independent: One paragraph on how diction shapes tone.

days.name: Wednesday
days.curriculum: Released FRQ 2 passage (nonfiction) — apply SPACE CAT + DIDLS to a new text.
days.learning_targets: I can transfer rhetorical-analysis skills to an unfamiliar passage.
days.do_now: Predict the speaker's purpose from the passage's title and first line.
days.learning_looks_like:
Explicit: Walk through the FRQ 2 prompt structure.
Student: Groups annotate the passage.
Independent (even week): MCQ practice set on the passage.

days.name: Thursday
days.curriculum: Full timed rhetorical-analysis essay (Week B — even week) on the FRQ 2 passage.
days.learning_targets: I can write a full rhetorical-analysis essay under timed conditions.
days.do_now: Draft a one-sentence defensible thesis for the FRQ 2 passage.
days.learning_looks_like:
Explicit: Review thesis + line-of-reasoning expectations.
Student: 2-minute thesis peer check.
Independent: 35-minute timed essay (AP conditions).
days.assessment: Summative — full timed rhetorical-analysis essay (1-6 rubric).

days.name: Friday
days.curriculum: Peer review + AP rubric scoring; Columnist Journal entry #2.
days.learning_targets: I can evaluate an essay against the 1-6 rubric and reflect on my own writing.
days.do_now: Write down one strength and one goal from yesterday's essay.
days.learning_looks_like:
Explicit: Model rubric scoring on an anchor paper.
Student: Peer review using the 1-6 rubric.
Independent: Columnist Journal entry #2 (SPACE CAT + DIDLS + pre-write).
days.assessment: Formative — peer review form + Columnist Journal entry.
